$$F_X:\mathbb R\to[0,1],\qquad F_X(x):=\mathbb P(X\le x)=\mathbb P_X((-\infty,x]).$$

The second expression is the same quantity written in terms of the law
[[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] of $X$.

Let $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a decreasing sequence of measurable sets for a measure $\mu$. If $\mu(E_{n_0})<+\infty$ for some $n_0$, then

$$\mu\left(\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n\right)=\inf_{n\in\mathbb N}\mu(E_n).$$

$$\mu\left(\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n\right)=\sup_{n\in\mathbb N}\mu(E_n).$$

No finiteness hypothesis is required.

Let $n\ge1$ be an integer, let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)$ be a measurable observation space, let $P$ be a probability law on it, and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be IID $P$-distributed sampling units ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]). For each $1\le k\le n$, let $T_k$ be a measurable real-valued statistic and write $\widehat\theta_k=T_k(Z_1,\ldots,Z_k)$; the target is a scalar $\theta(P)$ and $a_k>0$ is its declared normalization at sample size $k$. The empirical law
$$P_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{Z_i}$$
is a probability law by [[lem-finite-empirical-measure-is-a-probability-law]].

For an integer $1\le m\le n$, the **m-out-of-n bootstrap** draws $Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_m^*$ conditionally IID from $P_n$ and computes
$$R_{m,n}^{*}:=a_m\bigl(T_m(Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_m^*)-\widehat\theta_n\bigr).$$
The conditional distribution of this root given the observed sample is the bootstrap approximation. The ordinary n-out-of-n bootstrap is the case $m=n$ and uses $a_n$.

For $1\le m<n$, **subsampling without replacement** chooses a subset $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_m\}$ uniformly from the $\binom{n}{m}$ subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and computes
$$R_{m,n}^{\mathrm{sub}}:=a_m\bigl(T_m(Z_{i_1},\ldots,Z_{i_m})-\widehat\theta_n\bigr).$$
Its conditional law is the uniform distribution over those subsets. With replacement and without replacement are distinct conditional laws, even though both use the same declared statistic $T_m$.

The asymptotic regime considered on this page has integer $m=m_n\to\infty$ and $m_n/n\to0$. The resampled root uses the actual size-$m$ scale $a_m$; validity does not follow merely from this regime. For inference based on a centered root, the scale ratio $a_m/a_n\to0$ is an additional root-specific centering condition when it is used. A design with dependent sampling units requires a separate design-matched resampling procedure. This definition does not identify a bootstrap law with a Bayesian posterior or a design-randomization law. Extrapolation from several resample sizes is not asserted here; it requires a separate proof of the source-specific regular expansion and remainder regime.

Let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be random elements with the same measurable target $(E,\mathcal E)$. They are **identically distributed** if $\mathbb P(X_i\in B)=\mathbb P(X_j\in B)$ for all $i,j\in I$ and $B\in\mathcal E$, that is, their laws in [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] agree. They are **independent and identically distributed (IID)** if, in addition, the whole family is independent in [[def-independent-random-elements]]. Independence means mutual independence, not merely pairwise independence. No moment assumption is part of either definition. The empty family satisfies these universal conditions vacuously.

For Borel probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on a metric space S, write $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ if $\int f\,d\mu_n\to\int f\,d\mu$ for every bounded continuous real function f on S. statistical experiment as in [[def-statistical-experiment]], and assume

$C:\mathcal X\to\mathcal P(\Theta)$, where
$\mathcal P(\Theta):=\{A:A\subseteq\Theta\}$, such that, for every
$\eta\in\Theta$, its

$$C_\eta:=\{x\in\mathcal X:\eta\in C(x)\}$$
belongs to $\mathcal A$. Its **coverage at $\theta$** is
$c_C(\theta):=P_\theta(C_\theta)$, and its **confidence level** is
$\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}c_C(\theta)$, the greatest lower bound of those

$$E[X]=m,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(X)=\sigma^2.$$

in probability.

No completeness or coupling is required.

For $g_2(\mu)=\mu^2$, the derivative at zero vanishes and the second derivative is $2$, so [F5] gives the second-order scale $R_{n,2}=Z_n^2\Rightarrow Z^2$; directly, its law is exactly that of $Z^2$ for every $n$. For $g_1(\mu)=|\mu|$, the first-order delta premise fails at zero, and directly $R_{n,1}=|Z_n|$ has the law of $|Z|$ for every $n$. For $t>0$, the density bound in [F4] gives $P(|Z|\le t)\le2t/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and $P(Z^2\le t)\le2\sqrt t/\sqrt{2\pi}$; for $t<0$ both probabilities are zero. Therefore both true-root CDFs are continuous at zero and equal zero there. Their constant-law sequences converge weakly by [F8], and [F9] gives the same CDF limit at this continuity point.

By [F1], the bootstrap draws are conditionally IID from the empirical law and $W_n^*$ is the centered, $\sqrt n$-scaled empirical-bootstrap mean. By [F10], $G_n^*$ is the CDF of this conditional root law. The specialized supplier fact [F6] and the local CDF lemma [F7] give $\Delta_n:=\sup_x|G_n^*(x)-\Phi(x)|\to0$ in probability. For a realized value $z=Z_n$, the event $R_{n,1}^*\le0$ is $|z+W_n^*|\le|z|$, and the event $R_{n,2}^*\le0$ is $(z+W_n^*)^2\le z^2$; both are the same interval event, with $W_n^*\in[-2z,0]$ if $z\ge0$ and $W_n^*\in[0,-2z]$ if $z<0$. A uniform CDF error $\Delta_n$ also bounds the error at left limits, since $\Phi$ is continuous. Thus each conditional probability differs by at most $2\Delta_n$ from its standard-normal value $\Phi(2|Z_n|)-\frac12$.

Put $b:=\Phi(2)-\frac12>0$ and $c=b/2$. On $A_n:=\{|Z_n|\ge1\}$, whose probability is the fixed positive number $P(|Z|\ge1)$ by [F4], the normal interval probability in step 1.2 is at least $b$. On the additional event $\Delta_n\le b/4$, both conditional root CDFs at zero are therefore at least $c$. The true roots have the laws of $|Z|$ and $Z^2$ for every $n$ by [F4]. Their atom at zero is zero, and the standard-normal density is bounded by $(2\pi)^{-1/2}$, so for every $d>0$, $\mathbb E[h_d(|Z|)]\le P(|Z|<d)\le2d/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and $\mathbb E[h_d(Z^2)]\le P(|Z|<\sqrt d)\le2\sqrt d/\sqrt{2\pi}$, where $h_d(t)=1$ for $t\le0$, $h_d(t)=1-t/d$ for $0<t<d$, and $h_d(t)=0$ for $t\ge d$. Choose $d$ so both expectations are below $c/2$. For either bootstrap root, $\mathbb E^*[h_d(R_{n,j}^*)]\ge P^*(R_{n,j}^*\le0)\ge c$ on that event, while its true test integral is below $c/2$. The event has probability at least $P(|Z|\ge1)-P(\Delta_n>b/4)$, whose limit is positive. Thus the conditional integral of a bounded continuous test function fails to converge in probability to the true integral, contradicting conditional weak consistency.
